Drawdown threshold tradeoffs

Methods, limitations and provenance

The model uses a fixed hypothetical long USD1 million, PHP reporting, and published BSP observations. The rate is the USD row’s PHIL. PESO EQUIVALENT field; verified market-close one-day risk is not claimed.

Prior 99% Historical Simulation VaR uses the most recent 250 eligible original changes and the higher quantile. Signed loss is the negative of P&L. Exact signed loss must strictly exceed exact VaR for an exception. The near-tie review tolerance is PHP0.01 and never overrides strict classification.

Seven intervals crossing unresolved source dates are excluded from main training and backtesting. No missing-rate filling, return bridging or substitution is used. Source-date ordering, public availability, underlying economic dates and series-method continuity remain qualified. Formal operational adequacy, independence and causal market explanations are not established.

The running peak begins at the first study valuation and never resets yearly. A 3% episode starts on the first observed drawdown at or below −3%, continues while that condition holds, and ends on the first endpoint above −3%. Re-entry is a new episode; no extra minimum separation is imposed. Threshold exit is distinct from recovery to the peak. Later endpoints do not appear in the default selected-date charts.

No signal means only no trigger under these rules; unavailable is not zero. Stress scenarios do not bound losses or establish VaR adequacy. Any review remains manual.

Report provenance

Checks are documented consistency checks. The report is an educational historical prototype and does not claim independent bank-model certification. Notes remain in the browser unless exported; the export includes version, snapshot hash, dates and record identifiers.
